tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: We recognize deferred tax assets and liabilities to reflect the future tax consequences of events that have been recognized in the financial statements or tax returns. A deferred tax asset or liability results from the temporary difference between an item’s carrying value as reflected in the financial statements and its tax basis, and is calculated using enacted applicable tax rates. We assess the likelihood that our deferred tax assets will be recovered from future taxable income and, to the extent we believe that recovery is unable to reach the “more likely than not” standard, a valuation allowance is established. Changes in the valuation allowance, when recorded, are included in the provision for income taxes in the consolidated financial statements. We assess uncertainty regarding tax positions taken in previously filed returns and record reserves in accordance with the guidance under Accounting Standards Codification 740-10, "Accounting for Uncertainty in Income Taxes". We classify interest expense and penalties associated with taxes and uncertain tax positions as part of our provision for income taxes based upon applicable federal and state interest/underpayment percentages.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: We recognize deferred tax assets and liabilities to reflect the future tax consequences of events that have been recognized in the financial statements or tax returns. A deferred tax asset or liability results from the temporary difference between an item’s carrying value as reflected in the financial statements and its tax basis, and is calculated using enacted applicable tax rates. We assess the likelihood that our deferred tax assets will be recovered from future taxable income and, to the extent we believe that recovery is unable to reach the “more likely than not” standard, a valuation allowance is established. Changes in the valuation allowance, when recorded, are included in the provision for income taxes in the consolidated financial statements. We assess uncertainty regarding tax positions taken in previously filed returns and record reserves in accordance with the guidance under Accounting Standards Codification 740-10, "Accounting for Uncertainty in Income Taxes". We classify interest expense and penalties associated with taxes and uncertain tax positions as part of our provision for income taxes based upon applicable federal and state interest/underpayment percentages.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text:
Net cash flows provided by operating activities for the year ended December 31, 2025 was $477.0 million, compared to net cash flows provided by operating activities of $379.7 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, an increase of $97.3 million. Cash provided by operating activities for the year ended December 31, 2025 was attributable to net income of $432.4 million, adjusted for non-cash depreciation and amortization expenses of $86.5 million, non-cash operating lease expense of $63.2 million, and increases in trade accounts payable of $268.7 million and other current liabilities of $95.1 million, partially offset by increases in trade receivables of $243.2 million and merchandise inventory levels of $134.9 million, and a decrease in other non-current liabilities of $87.6 million.

The average number of days of sales in trade receivables for the quarter ended December 31, 2025 increased modestly compared to the same three-month period in 2024. The days in inventory increased modestly for the quarter ended December 31, 2025 compared to the quarter ended December 31, 2024.

lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Customers for our products and services are similarly diverse – we have approximately 150,000 customers, and our largest customer accounts for approximately 2% of our total sales.
During the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, domestic revenue accounted for 95 % of total revenue.
On a dollar volume basis, we filled approximately 60% of customer orders from this on-hand inventory in both 2025 and 2024.
Approximately 50% of the products we sold during 2025 were purchased from our top 25 suppliers.
We also rely on the information systems of third parties to achieve some of our business objectives.
These risks are also applicable where we rely on outside vendors to provide services, which typically operate in a cloud environment.
Approximately 50% of our purchases are made from only 25 manufacturers.
The value to our shareholders of our common stock depends on the regular payment of dividends, which are paid at the discretion of our Board of Directors.
